$about: PER-AXIS, PER-COMPONENT, BOTH NUMBERS AND THE DELTA. Generated, not typed:
every figure is read out of react-aria.json, base-ui.json, the API-translation
census, or probe.failure-taxonomy.json. `delta` is always base_ui MINUS react_aria,
so a negative number means Base UI scores lower — which is BETTER for a defect
count and WORSE for a line count. The sign is not a verdict; read the axis.
The two runs are the SAME harness file (experiments/harness/measure.mjs), unedited
between them. What differs is the impl-specific half it is pointed at:
specimens.<impl>.tsx and ledger.<impl>.json. The wrapped arm of the two specimens
files is identical component-for-component and prop-for-prop; the BARE arm composes
each library in its own vocabulary, and `supplied` states what a missing required
prop costs under each engine, which is not the same thing on the two sides.
ONE THING THE HARNESS COULD NOT MEASURE ON BOTH SIDES, stated so it is not read as
a null result: the React Aria arm can no longer be re-run. packages/ui/src holds the
Base UI port now, so `--impl react-aria` would measure Base UI source through the
React Aria specimens. react-aria.json is the frozen baseline and
experiments/baseline-rac/ is the source it was taken from; measure.mjs re-checks
that correspondence itself and records it per component as `provenance.identical`.

axis_1_ssr_defects.question: How many defects does the shipped, prerendered markup contain, graded by packages/gate's own RULES?
axis_1_ssr_defects.headline:
THE TOTAL IS THE SAME AND THE COMPOSITION IS COMPLETELY DIFFERENT — 4 either way,
and not one of the eight is the same defect.

React Aria's four are all `resolved-idrefs`, one each on select, menu, dialog and
popover: the useSlot/useSlotId pattern emits an aria-labelledby whose corrective
layout effect never runs on a server. Base UI has ZERO of them.

Base UI's four are all `named-controls`: switch (1), checkbox (2), number-field (1).
Three of them are the library's, one is the port's, and the difference matters:

  switch, checkbox   Base UI's Field.Label renders <label for=…> pointing at the
                     visually-hidden <input>, while the element that carries
                     role=switch / role=checkbox is a <span> that nothing names.
                     A <label> only names labelable elements, so containment does
                     not rescue it. PRESENT IN THE BARE ARM TOO — the wrapper
                     neither causes it nor can close it without an aria-label.
  number-field       Lumo's own. number-field.tsx renders form.tsx's <Label>, which
                     is a REACT ARIA component, inside a Base UI NumberField.Root.
                     RAC's Label reads LabelContext for its htmlFor and there is
                     none, so it emits a bare <label> and the <input> has no name.
                     The BARE arm, using Base UI's own Field.Label, is CLEAN — so
                     this one is a mixed-tree defect, not an upstream one.

axis_2_english_leaks.question: How much English does a Persian page serve, and what is holding it shut?
axis_2_english_leaks.headline:
Both wrappers serve ZERO English. The interesting numbers are the counterfactuals.

BARE LIBRARY, patches in place: React Aria 0, Base UI 4. That inversion is entirely
an artefact of the patch — RAC's 0 is what the fa-IR bundles bought. With the
patches removed the bare React Aria arm leaks 5 and the bare Base UI arm still
leaks 4, and those 4 are the ONLY English strings in the thirteen Base UI
components: aria-roledescription="Number field", aria-label="Increase",
aria-label="Decrease" (number-field) and aria-label="Dismiss" (combobox's
@internal ComboboxInternalDismissButton, open state only).

WITHOUT THE REQUIRED PROPS: 5 → 3. Two of React Aria's five were English strings
Base UI simply does not have — `selectPlaceholder` ("Select an item") and the
combobox's `buttonLabel`/`listboxLabel`. Base UI writes NOTHING there instead, and
that is why `controls_that_would_be_unnamed_without_required_props` is UNCHANGED at
11: the same props are still load-bearing, they are just holding back a different
defect. The select placeholder is a third case that is neither, recorded in the
specimens as `absent: "empty"` — an empty collapsed control, invisible to a gate
and to a reviewer alike.

Three of the four Base UI leaks are prop-reachable and closed. The fourth,
"Dismiss", is constructed with no props at all and is NOT reachable — the first
structurally unreachable English string in either library's V1 surface.
axis_2_english_leaks.caveat:
ATTRIBUTION ARTEFACT, stated so nobody reads it as a finding. The harness names a
leak's source by looking the English up in the PATCHES' key table, which is React
Aria's. Base UI's "Dismiss" therefore comes back annotated with
`patches/react-aria@3.51.0.patch → overlays.dismiss`. The COUNT is correct — it is
produced by the gate rule, not by the lookup — but that patch has nothing to do
with Base UI. It is a string collision, not a dependency.

axis_3_rtl.question: Who resolves direction, and does any of it happen in JavaScript?
axis_3_rtl.headline:
Zero class deltas on both sides: neither wrapper branches on direction in JS.
One style delta on both sides, and it is the slider's thumb both times — but the
two are not the same measurement, and this is the axis where the engines differ
most in KIND rather than in count.

  React Aria   the thumb's inline style is `left: 60%`, arithmetic RAC performed
               from useLocale().direction. Get the provider wrong and it is 40%.
  Base UI      the thumb's inline style is `inset-inline-start: 40%` plus
               `translate: 50% -50%`, and the BROWSER mirrors it. Under the LTR
               arm the translate is `-50% -50%`; the inset stays 40%.

The Base UI form is the better primitive — there is no direction-dependent
arithmetic to get wrong — but it is reached from a DIFFERENT source. React Aria
took direction from the locale; Base UI takes it from its own DirectionProvider,
which defaults to 'ltr' and knows nothing about the page's locale or its dir
attribute. slider.tsx mounts one from `direction(locale)`; tabs.tsx does NOT, and
records the gap: arrow keys on a Persian <Tabs> reverse only if the application
mounted a DirectionProvider, which nothing in the type system demands.

So the axis's number is flat and the risk moved: from 'a locale provider you must
mount' to 'a direction provider you must mount, per page, that no component can
supply and no compiler asks for'.

axis_4_wrapper_lines.question: How much of each wrapper is styling, and how much is correcting upstream?

api_translation_census.$note:
NOT in `correcting_lines`, on purpose. The ledgers hold one definition of
'correcting' across both arms — a line that fixes an upstream DEFECT — so that
`correcting_lines` compares like with like. The Base UI port also carries a large
body of pure API-translation code, which the harness's mechanical classifier puts
in `structure`. This census counts it directly, over BOTH arms, using exact
string shapes rather than judgement. See `patterns`.

shared_module_cost.$note:
A THIRD shared module the React Aria arm did not have, and the harness cannot see
it: measure.mjs reads exactly a component's `file` and `variantsFile`, so every
line of base-ui-adapter.ts is outside all four line counts above. It is counted
here whole, and its consequence for the copy-in distribution is under
`axis_7_distribution` — where it breaks the smoke gate for ten items.

axis_4_wrapper_lines.headline:
Code lines 1198 → 1930 (+732, +61%). Whole files 2493 → 3904 (+1411, +57%).
Styling is flat: 377 → 385 (+8), which is the experiment's control — the cva blocks
were reused byte-identical on purpose, so a large styling delta would have meant
the swap had leaked into the restyle it was supposed to exclude. It did not.

Correcting lines 89 → 106 (+17) under ONE unchanged definition of 'correcting'.
The composition moved more than the count:

  upstream-workaround  20 → 33  (+13)   the whole of the increase, essentially
  aria-fix             10 → 13   (+3)
  required-prop-shim   34 → 37   (+3)   the rule Lumo adds, unchanged in substance
  rtl-fix               5 →  6   (+1)
  ssr-fix               2 →  2    (0)
  type-narrowing       14 → 13   (−1)
  slot-claim            4 →  2   (−2)   slot=increment/decrement are gone: Base UI
                                        ships dedicated Increment/Decrement parts

Base UI needs MORE hand-written compensation and it needs it in different places:
three React contexts
(select's placeholder/label carrier, menu's submenu-level and onAction carriers),
three positional trigger splits (popover, tooltip, dialog), a native <label htmlFor>
with an SSR-stable useId (combobox), a DirectionProvider (slider) and a
getAriaValueText (slider).

AND THE REAL DELTA IS THE ONE THE LEDGER DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES: 7 API-translation
sites become 235, plus a 126-line shared adapter module that ten of the thirteen
import. That is what the +732 code lines are mostly made of.

axis_5_bundle_weight.question: What does each component cost a consumer, alone and marginally?
axis_5_bundle_weight.headline:
THE THREE NUMBERS POINT IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS AND ALL THREE ARE REAL.

  standalone sum        461,923 → 397,326 gzip  (−64,597, −14%)
  all thirteen together 103,666 → 111,070 gzip  (+7,404, +7%)
  marginal sum           40,938 →  55,950 gzip  (+15,012, +37%)

A component ALONE is usually cheaper on Base UI, because React Aria drags one large
shared runtime in behind whichever component you imported first. Eleven of the
thirteen shrink; tabs is the biggest fall (37,815 → 18,952, −50%). Two GROW, both
overlays: popover 30,255 → 43,918 (+45%) and tooltip 21,528 → 37,745 (+75%), where
Base UI's floating-ui positioning stack costs more standalone than RAC's did.

A whole design system is the opposite. Sharing is exactly what React Aria is good
at: 462 modules collapse to 103.7 KB. Base UI's 359 modules — FEWER modules — come
to 111.1 KB, because the components share less with each other. Hence the marginal
cost rising 37%: adding the fourteenth Base UI component to a project buys less
from what is already there.

AND THE ALL-THIRTEEN BUNDLE STILL CARRIES BOTH LIBRARIES. Measured module-by-module:
260 Base UI modules and 12 React Aria ones. Every one of the twelve arrives through
number-field.tsx → form.tsx, which is NOT one of the thirteen and still renders
RAC's <Label>, <Description> and <FieldError>. A real adoption pays that off; this
experiment's number does not, and the +7,404 should be read with that in it.

axis_6_maintenance_do_the_patches_still_.question: Does `pnpm verify` pass with the patches gone? Measured by neutralising `patchedDependencies`, reinstalling, and re-running every gate.
axis_6_maintenance_do_the_patches_still_.method:
1. Backed up pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml to a scratch dir with sha256.
2. Commented out the three `patchedDependencies` lines in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
3. `pnpm install --prefer-offline`. Verified the patch was OFF: packages/ui's
   react-aria-components resolves to a store path with no `_patch_hash` segment,
   and dist/private/intl/fa-IR.mjs is absent.
4. Ran every gate in `verify` individually rather than through `pnpm verify`,
   because verify short-circuits on the first failure and this branch already fails
   at gate:test — a single exit code would have said nothing about the patches.
5. Restored both files byte-for-byte (sha256 re-verified identical) and reinstalled.
6. Re-verified the restore: the patched store path is linked again, fa-IR.mjs is
   back, and the full @lumo-ui/ui suite is back to exactly 11 failures / 501 passed.
axis_6_maintenance_do_the_patches_still_.restore_note:
ONE THING TO KNOW IF YOU REPEAT THIS. After restoring the two files, `pnpm install`
reported «Already up to date» in 213ms and did NOT relink — pnpm 11 short-circuits
on `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`, and neither `--force` nor
`--frozen-lockfile` overrides it. Deleting that one file and reinstalling performed
the full relink (262 packages, 7.8s). A restore that is not verified by re-running a
patch-dependent test is not a restore: on this machine the un-relinked state was
indistinguishable from success at the shell.
axis_6_maintenance_do_the_patches_still_.answer:
NO — but not because of the patches, and that is the finding.

`pnpm verify` does not pass on this branch WITH the patches either. It fails at
gate:test, three gates before anything a patch could touch. So the patch question
has to be asked as a DELTA rather than as a pass/fail, and the delta is clean:

  removing the patches costs 26 additional test failures, and not one of them is
  in the thirteen components this experiment replaced.

gates.$order: verify runs: gate:types → gate:no-css-modules → gate:test → gate:registry → gate:smoke → gate:html

gate:types.note: The Base UI port type-checks across all 7 workspace projects under exactOptionalPropertyTypes. Patch-independent.

failures_added_by_removing_the_patches.note:
Every one is a component this experiment did NOT touch and that is still React
Aria. dates.test.tsx loses its «امروز» today-cell announcement, its «خالی» empty
segments, its per-family zero-English assertions and its four bundle-parity
checks; patch.test.tsx — the suite whose entire purpose is to prove the patch
reaches the SERVER render — loses all five; tree.test.tsx loses its «بستن» /
«باز کردن» expand button and its no-Latin-word assertion.

gate:registry.note: Patch-independent by construction: the generator reads component SOURCE and diffs registry.json; it never touches react-aria's intl bundles. See axis_7_distribution for what it found.

gate:smoke.note: Patch-independent by construction: it type-checks copied SOURCE in a bare temp project. Its failure is TS2307 on a relative import. See axis_7_distribution.

gate:html.detail: `next build` crashes before the gate CLI ever runs: «Error occurred prerendering page "/view/en-US/context-menu" … Base UI error #36». Byte-for-byte the same failure with and without the patches. Error #36 is the MenuRootContext throw — see the conformance taxonomy. The site cannot be built at all, so the HTML gate — the tier this project's whole defect ledger is measured at — produced NO data on this branch in either configuration.

do_the_thirteen_need_the_patches.measured_by: node experiments/harness/measure.mjs --impl base-ui --skip-tests --skip-bundle, run once with the patches installed and once without
do_the_thirteen_need_the_patches.note:
Not one of the thirteen Base UI components' numbers moves when the patches are
removed — SSR defects, English counts, bare-arm counts, all identical. The
patches are irrelevant to them, which is the strongest form the maintenance
argument can take FOR these thirteen.

It does not generalise to the library. The patch files add 33 fa-IR bundles
across two packages and the 26 tests that fail without them belong to Calendar,
the date family, Breadcrumbs and Tree — none of which Base UI has been shown to
replace here, and one of which (Calendar) DECISIONS §0 chose React Aria FOR,
because @internationalized/date ships PersianCalendar and nothing else does.

axis_7_distribution.question: Do the thirteen still ship? Lumo distributes by copy-in, and two gates grade exactly that.
axis_7_distribution.$note: Measured WITH the patches in place, so nothing here is attributable to axis 6. Both failures are new on this branch.

gate:registry.what_happened: `node scripts/build-registry.mjs && git diff --exit-code registry.json` — the generator ran, rewrote registry.json (31 insertions, 14 deletions across 107 items) and the diff check failed. registry.json is therefore MODIFIED in the working tree; it was left that way deliberately, because it is the evidence.

findings.finding: Ten items declare an unresolvable registryDependency
findings.cause: build-registry.mjs maps a `./x.tsx` import to the registry item `x`, with one special case that rewrites `x.variants.ts` to its owner `x`. `./base-ui-adapter.ts` matches neither, so it is emitted verbatim — and there is no item by that name among the 107.

findings.finding: ZERO items declare @base-ui/react as an npm dependency
findings.cause: `EXTERNAL` in build-registry.mjs is an exact-match Set of bare specifiers. Base UI is imported by SUBPATH — `@base-ui/react/button`, `@base-ui/react/menu` — so even adding the package name to the set would not match. A consumer copying `button` today receives a file importing a package nothing tells them to install.
findings.severity: silent — the smoke gate fails on the adapter first, so this one is not what turns the build red

gate:smoke.what_happened: 107 items were copied into a bare project and type-checked as a consumer receives them. Ten failed with TS2307 «Cannot find module './base-ui-adapter.ts'»: button, checkbox, dialog, number-field, popover, slider, switch, tabs, toggle, tooltip.
gate:smoke.note: This is the cost base-ui-adapter.ts's own header predicted in prose, now measured: «Lumo ships by copy-in … On Base UI it would also travel with this». It does not travel with it, and the gate that exists to catch exactly this caught it.

conformance.question: What do the Lumo suites say, and for every failure: missing capability, different DOM shape, or real accessibility regression?

union.note: The harness's union is the suites that DIRECTLY import one of the thirteen, plus coverage.test.ts. Same 10 files on both sides.

whole_package_suite.$note: Run separately, outside the harness, because the union above is a subset. It confirms the union caught every failure: the full 29-file @lumo-ui/ui suite fails the SAME 11 and no others.

components_without_a_behavioural_suite.note:
THE SAME FIVE ON BOTH SIDES, and it is the most important caveat on this axis.
switch, checkbox, popover, tooltip and number-field have NO test file that imports
them, so their 0/0 is not a passed conformance bar — nothing behavioural ran
against the replacement at all. Three of the four new SSR defects (switch 1,
checkbox 2) and the wholly unannounced tooltip live in exactly this set. A green
column here is the vacuous pass this repository's gate rules exist to prevent.

$legend.missing-capability: The behaviour or composition no longer works. The suite is right and the code is worse.
$legend.different-dom-shape: The suite asserts a React Aria internal — an attribute NAME, a physical inline style, a count of an upstream defect. The fact it was guarding is still true, stated another way, and VERIFIED to be so below. Noise.
$legend.accessibility-regression: A real defect in the accessibility tree. Signal.

taxonomy.$verified_by: experiments/measurements/probe.failure-taxonomy.json — four render probes that ask what the failing assertions could not.

failures.test: is role=alertdialog, labelled by the Persian title, with zero English spoken
failures.detail:
role=alertdialog with NO accessible name: aria-labelledby is null AND aria-label is
null, while the <h2> is present and carries its own generated id. RAC's useDialog
pointed the dialog's aria-labelledby at whatever claimed slot="title" through
HeadingContext; DialogHeading is now Base UI's Dialog.Title, which writes its id
into a Base UI Dialog.Root store that this composition does not have.
SCOPE: alert-dialog.tsx is NOT one of the thirteen. It is collateral — a still-RAC
component that composes a ported one.

failures.test: cancel closes without confirming; confirm runs onConfirm and then closes
failures.detail:
Neither verb closes the dialog. AlertDialog takes `close` from RAC's Dialog
children-render-prop, which resolves through OverlayTriggerStateContext — and the
surrounding DialogTrigger/DialogOverlay/DialogModal are Base UI now, so there is no
such state in the tree and `close` is a no-op. Measured: open before cancel true,
open after cancel true.
SCOPE: collateral, as above.

failures.test: the first byte holds the surface and nothing of the menu
failures.assertion: Error: Base UI: MenuRootContext is missing. Menu parts must be placed within <Menu.Root>.
failures.detail:
A hard throw, not a failed assertion. context-menu.tsx is still React Aria and
implements the virtual-trigger pattern itself, rendering `MenuPopover` + `Menu`
into a portal it owns; `MenuPopover` is now Base UI's Menu.Portal, which calls
useMenuRootContext() non-optionally. RAC's Popover degraded in the same position.
This is the same error that kills the site build — Base UI error #36 while
prerendering /view/en-US/context-menu — so it is not confined to the suite.
SCOPE: collateral; context-menu.tsx is not one of the thirteen.

failures.test: Slider — places the thumb from the INLINE-END edge on a Persian page
failures.detail:
NOISE, verified rather than assumed. The test pinned React Aria's ARITHMETIC, not
the placement: RAC computed left:60% from useLocale().direction. Base UI writes
inset-inline-start:40% with translate:50% -50% and lets the browser mirror it —
the same position, expressed logically, and 40% from the reading start IS 60% from
the physical left. The accessibility tree is intact too: aria-valuenow=40,
aria-valuetext=۴۰ (Persian digits), aria-label=بودجه.

failures.test: a plain modal dialog is clean; isDismissable on the OVERLAY adds one 'Dismiss'
failures.detail: NOISE, and an improvement. The suite PINNED an upstream defect — RAC's non-prop-reachable visually-hidden <button aria-label="Dismiss">. Base UI dismisses by listener rather than by focusable sentinel and emits none, so the test fails by finding zero English where it demanded one.

failures.test: every open popover carries exactly two unreachable 'Dismiss' labels
failures.detail: NOISE, same cause as above. Two unreachable English strings became zero.

failures.test: MenuItem keeps typeahead text and marks submenus with an aria-hidden mirrored glyph
failures.detail:
NOISE, verified. `data-has-submenu` is React Aria's NAME for the fact; Base UI
states the same fact as aria-haspopup="menu" + aria-expanded="false", both
measured present — and aria-haspopup is the one an assistive technology actually
reads. The rest of the same test case, which never got to run, also holds: the
mirrored glyph is still «›» on an aria-hidden element, and the first item's
typeahead text is still «کپی».

failures.test: carries `data-selected` for the ON state, not `data-pressed`
failures.detail:
NOISE FOR THE ACCESSIBILITY TREE, SIGNAL FOR THE PIXELS, and the two must not be
collapsed. aria-pressed="true" is emitted, so a screen reader is told the toggle
is on. But the two libraries use the SAME WORD for OPPOSITE things — React Aria's
data-pressed is the transient pointer-down state and data-selected is ON; Base UI
emits data-pressed FOR the ON state and no data-selected at all. toggle.variants.ts
is reused byte-identical and styles ON through data-selected:, which now matches
nothing, so an ON toggle renders identically to an OFF one. Nothing errors.

conformance.summary:
323 → 323 cases in the harness's union; 323 passed → 312 passed, 0 failed → 11 failed.

  6 of 11 are REAL LOSSES  — 5 missing-capability + 1 accessibility-regression
  5 of 11 are NOISE        — the suite asserts a React Aria internal that Base UI
                             states another way, verified case by case

And the distribution of the six matters more than the count: ALL SIX are in
components OUTSIDE the thirteen (alert-dialog.tsx ×2, context-menu.tsx ×4) that
compose ported ones. Not one of the thirteen fails its own suite — because five of
the thirteen have no suite at all, and the four SSR defects that axis 1 found sit
in three of those five. The suites did not catch the regressions; the gate rules did.

limitations: SERVED BYTES ONLY. Every overlay in React Aria portals its content and renders null on the server, so a forced-open Select/Menu/Dialog/Popover/Tooltip contributes its TRIGGER's changed attributes and nothing else. Defects inside an overlay's own subtree (RAC's two unreachable DismissButtons, the listbox's aria-label) are NOT in these counts. packages/ui/src/overlays.test.tsx is the tier that covers them and it pins those numbers already.

ComboBox cannot be forced open at all: react-stately 3.49.0 nulls isOpen/defaultOpen inside useComboBoxState (dist/private/combobox/useComboBoxState.mjs:121). Its open render is byte-identical to its closed one and `open_state_reached` says so.

The RTL pass changes the LOCALE, which is the only lever that reaches a server render. A `dir` attribute cannot change server output — it is resolved by CSS at paint time — so a zero class-delta is the expected result for logical utilities, not a null result. The static census is the other half of that answer.

The English-leak attribution is a string match against the patch's own fa-IR values and the specimen's declared props. A Persian string that a component hardcodes and that also happens to be a patched value would be misattributed; none of the thirteen do this, and `supplied` is checked first so props always win.
Utility censuses are string matches over source, not a CSS parse.

Five of the thirteen — switch, checkbox, popover, tooltip, number-field — have NO test file that imports them, so `conformance.per_component` reports 0/0 for them and the only thing that would run against a replacement is coverage.test.ts, which checks wiring and English defaults rather than behaviour. `components_without_a_behavioural_suite` names them. Treating their green as a passed conformance bar would be the vacuous pass this project's gate rules exist to prevent.

base-ui.json carries measure.mjs's own hardcoded `limitations` array verbatim, and ONE entry is wrong for this arm: «ComboBox cannot be forced open at all: react-stately 3.49.0 nulls isOpen/defaultOpen». The observation still holds — `open_state_reached` is false — but the cause moved from the library to Lumo. Base UI's Combobox.Root HAS a working `defaultOpen` (AriaCombobox.d.mts:46); the rebuilt `ComboBoxProps` no longer declares one, so the prop is never forwarded. The harness could not be edited to say so, so it is said here. The BARE arm does open, which is what makes the difference visible in the data.
base-ui.json's `versions` block does not name @base-ui/react: measure.mjs asks for a fixed list of five package ids. The version is 1.7.0 and is recorded under `versions.base_ui_engine` here.

`provenance.identical` is false for all thirteen in base-ui.json, as it must be — experiments/baseline-rac/ holds the React Aria originals and the source has been replaced. That flag is doing its job, not reporting drift.

The React Aria arm cannot be re-run: packages/ui/src holds the Base UI port, so react-aria.json is a frozen baseline. measure.mjs re-checks each file against experiments/baseline-rac/ and reports it per component as `provenance.identical`.
`api_translation_census` is a string census over source, not a parse. Its patterns are listed and each is counted separately so any one can be discarded.

`gate:registry` and `gate:smoke` were measured WITH the patches only. They read component source and registry.json and never touch react-aria's intl bundles, so they are patch-independent by construction — but that is an argument, not a measurement, and it is labelled as one.

gate:html produced no data on either configuration: `next build` crashes on /view/en-US/context-menu before the gate CLI runs. The tier this project's defect ledger actually lives at is therefore UNMEASURED on this branch, and no claim here should be read as covering it.

The specimens' `absent` field gains a third value, `"empty"`, for Base UI's Select placeholder — neither English nor unnamed. measure.mjs counts only `"english"` and `"unnamed"`, so the value lands in neither counterfactual and survives in the per-record data. That is deliberate; recording it as either would have inflated a headline.
